title: Broadcast Receivers
objectives: Know the modern restrictions on implicit broadcasts

sections.markdown: A BroadcastReceiver responds to system-wide or app events (connectivity changes, boot completed, battery low). It's a publish-subscribe mechanism between components and apps.
Since Android 8, most **implicit** broadcasts can no longer be declared in the manifest (battery drain). Register them at runtime, or use explicit broadcasts/WorkManager/observers instead.
Doing long work in onReceive — it runs on the main thread and the receiver is killed shortly after returning. Hand off to WorkManager or a coroutine; don't block.
For in-app events, prefer a LiveData/Flow/observer pattern over LocalBroadcastManager (deprecated). Use system broadcasts only for genuine system events.

flashcards.back: Manifest receivers persist even when the app isn't running (limited events); context-registered ones live only while registered.
